result.process_summary: In both the puppy‑training scenario and reinforcement learning, an agent repeatedly interacts with an environment, takes actions, receives feedback (reward or penalty), and updates its behavior so that actions leading to higher cumulative reward become more frequent.
potential_breaks: The analogy treats the absence of a treat as a penalty, conflating no reward with negative reward, which are distinct in RL.
Puppy learning often involves innate motivations and shaping, whereas RL agents rely purely on algorithmic updates.
Rewards in the analogy are immediate, while RL can involve delayed or sparse rewards.
